result:
The architect's report is in `.feature-flow/rate-limit/architect.md`. It proposes one design and says no real alternative exists, so I need your confirmation before I write `design.md`.

**Recommended: a locked sliding-window log file per caller**

- **Storage:** each caller gets a flat file listing one epoch timestamp per request. The files live under `RATE_LIMIT_STATE_DIR`, which defaults to `/tmp/rate-limit-state`.
- **Handling two requests at once:** each call takes a lock by creating a directory with `mkdir`. If a crashed process left the lock behind, the next call takes it over. A trap on exit and on interrupt/terminate signals releases the lock.
- **What each call does:** drop timestamps older than `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS`, count the rest against `RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, add its own timestamp, then print `ok` or `denied`. The file is rewritten through a temp file and `mv`, so it is never half-written.
- **Tests:** `tests/test.sh` uses its own temporary state directory and small limit/window values, so AC1–AC3 are checked the same way every run.

**Why only one option:** the spec needs three things together:
- the count survives between separate runs of the script;
- the window is truly rolling;
- nothing new is required, such as a daemon or an external tool.

Every other shape the architect looked at gives up one of these:
- a counter that resets at fixed time slots isn't a rolling window;
- lock-free marker files don't give a reliable count when two requests arrive together;
- sqlite or a daemon adds a new dependency.

**My recommendation:** confirm it. It matches the constraints you signed off on. The only new thing the spec doesn't mention is the `RATE_LIMIT_STATE_DIR` override.

Reply **confirm**, or tell me what you object to. If you object, I'll send your objection back to the architect for one more pass.
